before.ru: Она поблагодарила её за предложение помощи.
before.en: She thanked her for the offer of help.

after.en: She said thank you for the offer of help.

before.en_text: to come along (with sb/to a place)
before.en: Would you like to come to the beach tomorrow?

after.en: Would you like to come along to the beach tomorrow?
after.ru: Хочешь пойти с нами на пляж завтра?

before.en: I happened to say the wrong thing.

after.en: I accidentally said the wrong thing.

before.en_text: to have enough, to get one's fill
before.ru: Дети наели достаточно торта на вечеринку.
before.en: The children had enough cake for the party.

after.en: The children had plenty of cake at the party.
after.ru: На празднике дети вдоволь наелись торта.

regenerated.en masse: Audit: "Der kom mennesker en masse" is a marked, old-fashioned order. Use the everyday "en masse" + noun: "Der kom en masse mennesker til koncerten."
regenerated.have på: Audit: "Jeg har på en varm jakke" is wrong — with an object the particle follows it ("har en jakke på"), which splits the phrase. Use a sentence where "have på" stays together naturally: a question with the object fronted ("Hvad skal jeg have på i aften?") or no object ("Hun havde ikke noget varmt på" is split too — avoid it).
